content.overview: Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 makes a marriage voidable (valid until annulled) on the grounds of non-consummation owing to the respondent’s impotence, contravention of s. 5(ii) (mental capacity), consent obtained by force or fraud, or pregnancy of the respondent by another person at the time of marriage. Strict statutory bars apply to the force/fraud and pregnancy grounds.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Which s. 12(1) ground? (2) Valid until annulled? (3) For (c)/(d) — one-year and cohabitation bars clear? (4) vs void s. 11?

sections.heading: Four voidability grounds
sections.body: (a) impotence/non-consummation; (b) s. 5(ii) mental capacity; (c) force or fraud; (d) pregnancy by another at marriage.

sections.heading: Valid until annulled
sections.body: Unlike s. 11 void marriages, a voidable marriage produces full marital status until the decree of nullity.

sections.heading: Mandatory bars under s. 12(2)
sections.body: Force/fraud and pregnancy grounds are tightly conditioned by one-year limitation and cohabitation/intercourse bars. Non-compliance bars the petition.

sections.heading: Children
sections.body: Children of an annulled voidable marriage receive the same limited legitimacy under s. 16 as children of a void marriage.

sections.heading: Contrast with s. 11
sections.body: s. 11: void ab initio, three s. 5 conditions. s. 12: valid until annulled, different grounds and strict bars.

examples.title: Impotence
examples.body: Non-consummation owing to respondent’s impotence at marriage and continuing — voidable under s. 12(1)(a); valid until decree.

examples.title: Force/fraud barred by cohabitation
examples.body: Fraud discovered, but petitioner continues full-consent cohabitation — petition under s. 12(1)(c) barred by s. 12(2).

hypotheticals.question: Are the one-year bars under s. 12(2) directory?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. They are mandatory conditions of maintainability for force/fraud and pregnancy grounds.

distinctions.title: Voidable (s. 12) vs Void (s. 11)
distinctions.left: Valid until annulled; impotence, s. 5(ii), force/fraud, pregnancy.
distinctions.right: Void ab initio; living spouse, prohibited degrees, sapinda.

rows.left: Strict one-year and cohabitation bars for (c)/(d).

misconceptions.trap: Voidable and void marriages are the same.
misconceptions.correction: Voidable is valid until annulled; void is a nullity from the beginning.
They are mandatory conditions of maintainability for force/fraud and pregnancy.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Four grounds; valid until annulled; s. 12(2) bars for force/fraud and pregnancy; contrast s. 11.
